definitions.explanation: A very steep or vertical rock face. Used for natural cliffs and metaphorically for extreme, precarious situations.

examples.japanese: {絶壁|ぜっぺき}から{海|うみ}を{見下|みお}ろした。
examples.english: I looked down at the sea from the cliff.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}の{片側|かたがわ}は{切|き}り{立|た}った{絶壁|ぜっぺき}だった。
examples.english: One side of the road was a sheer cliff.

examples.japanese: ロッククライマーたちが{絶壁|ぜっぺき}に{挑|いど}んでいる{姿|すがた}は{圧巻|あっかん}だった。
examples.english: The sight of the rock climbers tackling the sheer cliff face was spectacular.

notes:
USAGE:
{絶壁|ぜっぺき} emphasizes the extreme steepness or verticality of a cliff. Compare with {崖|がけ} (cliff, general) which does not necessarily imply a vertical face.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {切|き}り{立|た}った{絶壁|ぜっぺき} (a sheer, towering cliff)
- {断崖|だんがい}{絶壁|ぜっぺき} (precipitous cliff — a set phrase combining two near-synonyms for emphasis)
- {絶壁|ぜっぺき}をよじ{登|のぼ}る (to scramble up a cliff face)

SLANG:
In casual speech, {絶壁|ぜっぺき} is sometimes used humorously to describe the back of someone's head when it is very flat ({後頭部|こうとうぶ}が{絶壁|ぜっぺき}).
